name: Te Āpiti Manawatū Gorge Track
description:
The bush tracks through Te Āpiti, the Manawatū Gorge, are the best walking near Palmerston North. From the Western Gateway car park at 1631 Napier Road near Ashhurst, walk under the highway bridge and follow the signs to the Tawa Loop, about 4km and 1 hour 40 minutes, with a lookout over Palmerston North and a 6.2m carving of Whātonga where it meets the original track.

The full Manawatū Gorge Track runs 11.2km one way to Ballance Gorge Road near Woodville and takes 3 to 5 hours, so you need a car at each end or someone to pick you up. There are toilets at both ends and about halfway, and lookouts along the way over the river, the road, the railway and the wind farms on the ridges. Dogs aren't allowed anywhere in the reserve, and bikes aren't allowed on the walking tracks.
Local tip: The Western Gateway car park gates are locked at 9pm in summer and 7pm in winter, so leave plenty of time for the full walk. If you do get locked in, call the city council on 06 356 8199, but release fees apply.
hoursNote: Western Gateway car park open 5am to 9pm Oct to Apr, 6am to 7pm May to Sep; free; no dogs or bikes on walking tracks

name: NZ Rugby Museum
description:
The national rugby museum holds New Zealand's biggest collection of rugby memorabilia and records, about 50,000 items in all, from early jerseys and boots to All Blacks history. It's on the first floor of the Te Manawa complex at 326 Main Street, and it's open daily from 10am to 4pm.

New Zealand residents pay $15 for adults, $6 for children 5 to 17 and $40 for a family, and overseas visitors pay $25 for adults and $60 for a family. Gold Card holders and students pay $13. The Have a Go area lets you test your kicking, tackling, leaping, sprinting and scrum pushing.
Local tip: Allow at least an hour, and more if you're a fan, as the people who run it love a yarn about the game.
hoursNote: Open daily 10am to 4pm; closed Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year's Day and Good Friday

name: Te Awahou Nieuwe Stroom and De Molen
description:
This riverside cultural centre at 92 Main Street, Foxton, tells two stories side by side: Piriharakeke, a centre for Māori weaving, taonga and modern art, and Oranjehof, about Dutch settlers in New Zealand. There's also the Māpuna Kabinet art gallery, a library and heritage centre, and a café, and entry is by donation. It's open weekdays 9am to 4pm and weekends 10am to 3pm.

Next door, De Molen is a full size replica of a 17th century Dutch windmill with working millstones that grind flour on site. You can climb three floors to see the sails and gears up close for a gold coin donation ($3 per person, $10 for a family of four), or take a guided tour for $5. The Dutch Deli downstairs, open daily 9am to 4pm, sells the stone ground flour, Dutch cheeses, stroopwafels and souvenirs.
Local tip: The windmill's upper floors close at 3.30pm, so arrive by 3pm to climb it, then have a Dutch lunch at Café De Molen.
hoursNote: Te Awahou Mon to Fri 9am to 4pm, Sat and Sun 10am to 3pm; De Molen and Dutch Deli daily 9am to 4pm; free entry

name: Te Manawa Museum
description:
Te Manawa is Palmerston North's free museum and art gallery at 326 Main Street, a short walk from The Square. It mixes regional history and taonga with hands-on discovery spaces for kids and a changing programme of art exhibitions.

Current shows include Kura Te Waru-Rewiri (until 28 March 2027) and Pūtake: The source and foundation (until 21 February 2027). General entry is free with donations welcome, and some exhibitions cost extra. It's open daily from 10am to 5pm (1pm on Anzac Day), and closed on Good Friday, Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day. There's no café, but coffee is sold at set times, and there's paid parking on Main Street out front.
Local tip: The NZ Rugby Museum is in the same complex, so it's easy to do both on a wet afternoon.
hoursNote: Open daily 10am to 5pm; opens 1pm on Anzac Day; closed Good Friday, 25 and 26 Dec and 1 Jan; free entry

name: Victoria Esplanade
description:
The Esplanade is Palmerston North's big riverside park and gardens, and an easy place to spend a few hours. Highlights are the Dugald MacKenzie Rose Garden, with more than 5,000 roses, the tropical Peter Black Conservatory, and Wildbase Recovery, where a free walkthrough aviary has native birds and tuatara.

Kids get the biggest playground in the Manawatū and a summer paddling pool. The Esplanade Scenic Railway, a 2.2km miniature train, runs from 1pm to 4pm on weekends and public and school holidays, at $3 return. Mini golf, open 10am to 5pm, is $8 for adults, $4 for children or $20 for a family, and Café Esplanade is in the old post office in the middle of the park. The gates are open 8am to 9pm from October to March and 8am to 6pm the rest of the year.
Local tip: Join the Manawatū River Pathway from the park's river edge for a flat walk or bike ride along the river.
hoursNote: Gates open 8am to 9pm Oct to Mar, 8am to 6pm Apr to Sep; free entry; train and mini golf weekends and holidays

name: The Square, Te Marae o Hine
description:
The Square is the seven hectare green heart of Palmerston North, ringed by shops and cafés. The clock tower in the middle is the city's landmark, and around it are lawns, a duck pond, flower beds, Māori carvings, statues and Robert Jahnke's sculpture Ngā Huruhuru Rangatira (the feathers of the chief) at the Church Street corner.

The park's Māori name, Te Marae o Hine, often translated as the courtyard of the daughter of peace, was chosen to represent all peoples living together in peace, and the council has used both names since 2020. It's a pleasant spot for a picnic or a break between Te Manawa, a few minutes' walk away on Main Street, and the shops.
Local tip: Pho Nem Hanoi, at 68 The Square, is a good cheap lunch afterwards (closed Sundays).

name: Feilding Farmers Market and Saleyard Tour
description:
Friday is the day to visit Feilding. The farmers market fills Manchester Square under the town clocktower every Friday from 8.30am to 1pm, rain or shine, with up to 30 local growers and producers and live music. It was named New Zealand Farmers Market of the Year three years running, from 2012 to 2014.

Just down the street, the Feilding saleyards, the biggest in the country, have been selling sheep and cattle since 1880. A guided tour runs every Friday at 11am for at least an hour, led by retired local farmers. Tours are $15 for adults, $10 for students and $5 for children 12 and under, or $8 each for groups of six or more. Meet at the Drover and Dog silhouette outside the saleyards at 18 Manchester Street.
Local tip: Book the tour on 06 323 3318 and arrive 15 minutes early, then wander back to the market for lunch.
hoursNote: Market Fridays 8.30am to 1pm; saleyard tour Fridays 11am, adults $15, students $10, children $5

name: Foxton Beach
description:
Foxton Beach is a laid back seaside settlement at the mouth of the Manawatū River, about 5km west of Foxton. The wide west coast beach is used for swimming, surfing, fishing and kite boarding.

The river estuary is a Ramsar protected international wetland, where godwits, wrybills, Caspian terns and royal spoonbills gather on their migrations. Holben (Te Wharangi) Reserve, on Seabury Avenue next to the holiday park, has a playground, skate park, BMX track, bike skills area, basketball courts, picnic tables and toilets.
Local tip: Grab fish and chips from Delish Takeaways at 62A Seabury Avenue for a picnic at Holben Reserve.
hoursNote: Free; toilets at the main beach car park on Marine Parade South

name: Knead Bakery
description:
A small independent bakery in Hokowhitu Village, a short drive east of the city centre, run by Joel and Milly Young since 2022, and many locals now call it the best in Palmerston North. The cabinet is full of pies, croissants, Danish pastries, cinnamon scrolls, cream filled doughnuts and sourdough, and the coffee is good too.

It's popular, so the queue sometimes snakes out the door, but it moves quickly. Check its opening hours before you go.
Local tip: Ask about the cronut of the week, and go early for the best choice.
hoursNote: Tue to Fri 6.45am to 4pm, Sat 7.30am to 2.30pm; closed Sun and Mon

name: Pho Nem Hanoi Home Cooking
description:
A small Vietnamese restaurant at 68 The Square, serving Hanoi style home cooking. The menu runs from beef noodle soups to net spring rolls and chicken and avocado rice paper rolls, with vegetarian options such as tofu and vegetable noodle soup, and service stays quick even when it's busy.

It's open for lunch and dinner Monday to Saturday and closed on Sundays, but listings disagree on exact times, so phone 06 260 1051 to check. It also does takeaway and delivery.
Local tip: Friday nights are busy, so come early or order takeaway, and pick up a bag of their tea at the counter on the way out.
hoursNote: Mon to Fri 11am to 2.30pm and 5pm to 8pm, Sat to 8.30pm; closed Sun

name: Highway Takeaways and Foxton Roasts
description:
A fish and chip and roast takeaway on the state highway through Foxton, a handy stop on the drive through.

Check its current opening hours before you go.
Local tip: Take your parcel to Te Awahou Riverside Cultural Park, a few minutes away beside De Molen, where there are picnic tables.
hoursNote: Daily 9am to 7.30pm, to 8pm Fri and Sat

name: Ashhurst Domain Campground
description:
A council campground in the big riverside Ashhurst Domain, close to the Manawatū Gorge and the Te Āpiti tracks. Sites are $8 per person non-powered and $12 per person powered, and children are $6. You pay by cash or internet banking, and there's no booking, so just find a spot and check in at the office.

The campground was upgraded in 2025 and has a small kitchen and pay per use hot showers ($3 for up to five minutes by payWave). The domain around it has picnic and barbecue areas with toilets nearby, playgrounds, walking tracks and popular river swimming spots in summer. Dogs must be on a leash in the campground and aren't allowed in the playground, sportsgrounds or wetland. The maximum stay is 28 days in any three months.
Local tip: The council advises staying out of the river for 72 hours after rain. Large groups should phone 06 356 8199 ahead.
hoursNote: No booking; $8pp non-powered, $12pp powered, children $6; showers $3; max 28 days in 3 months

name: Tōtara Reserve Regional Park Campgrounds
description:
Two quiet campgrounds, Kererū and Kahikatea, in a bush reserve beside the Pohangina River in the Pohangina Valley, north east of Palmerston North. Horizons Regional Council runs them from Labour Weekend to Easter, with non-powered sites from $16 a night for two people and powered sites from $37.

Both have toilets, hot showers and electric barbecues, and Kererū has easy river access for swimming plus an adventure playground. Nature trails start behind the campgrounds, and walking tracks leave from Pohangina Valley East Road, though the Gilchrist Track is permanently closed after Cyclone Gabrielle. Dogs aren't allowed anywhere in the reserve.
Local tip: Book online before you go in summer, swim only at the Kererū site, and stay out of the river for three days after heavy rain.
hoursNote: Open Labour Weekend to Easter; from $16 per night for 2; bookings required; no dogs

name: Himatangi Beach Freedom Camping
description:
Free council camping in the recreation reserve car park at Himatangi Beach, a small, quiet west coast beach settlement west of Palmerston North. Manawatū District Council allows up to three vehicles overnight here, and it's one of its sites open to non-self-contained vehicles as well as certified self-contained ones (with a green warrant since 7 June 2026). It's for vehicles only, not tents.

You can stay up to five nights in any 30 days. The reserve has toilets open 24 hours, a playground, a picnic area, a skate area and basketball and tennis courts. Campers without their own toilet must use the public ones. Dogs aren't allowed in the playground.
Local tip: With only three spaces, arrive in the afternoon, and check the council's freedom camping map for any changes before you go.
hoursNote: Max 3 vehicles overnight; self-contained and non-self-contained allowed; 24 hour toilets; free
